title: Man. Post. Cap. X: GAR — tree gone, but the ban’s punishing force still reaches posterity (cross parallel)
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles answers the ‘law is gone’ point: the tree is gone, so the ban no longer lasts as a fruit-prohibition; yet the law’s force still lasts as the threat of punishing Adam’s disobedience—and that punishment was to lie not on Adam only but to flow to all posterity. So too Christ on the cross-tree bore the curse by the force of ‘cursed is he who hangs on a tree’ (Gal 3:13). The cross is gone and that law does not last; yet the merit of the obedience he rendered on that cursed cross flows to us by free imputation to the world’s end.
pass_b_english: GAR. To the argumentation that that law for some thousands of years now is no more, etc., the reply is: neither does the Tree still stand, nor therefore does that law endure insofar as it regarded the prohibition of that forbidden fruit; yet the force of the law still perseveres insofar as it threatened punishment for that disobedience of Adam which was to lie not on Adam only, but also to flow out upon all posterity.

Just as Christ too was taken on the tree of the Cross, and there bore the curse, by the force and prescription of that law constituted by God, Cursed is he who hangs on a tree, as Paul teaches in Galatians 3:13.

The Cross has been taken away, and that law does not endure; and yet the merit of the obedience which Christ rendered on that cursed Cross flows to us by free imputation, and will flow to the end of the world.
source_text: GAR. Ad argumentationem, lex illa iam ab aliquot annorum millibus non est amplius &c. Resp. Nec Arborem exstare amplius, neque adeo legem illam perdurare, quatenus respiciebat prohibitionem fructus illius vetiti; sed vim tamen legis perseverare, quatenus inobedientiae illi Adami punitionem interminabatur quae non Adamo tantum incubitura, verum etiam in omnes posteros dimanatura esset. Sicut etiam Christus in arbore Crucis direptus est, & ibi maledictionem pertulit, ex vi & praescripto legis illius a Deo constitutae, Maledictus qui pendet in ligno, ut docet Paulus Galat. iii. 13. Sublata est Crux, & lex illa non perdurat; & tamen obedientiae, quam Christus in maledicta illa Cruce praestitit, meritum ad nos imputatione gratuita dimanat, & ad mundi finem dimanaturum est.
